invariants.rationale: Complete information first exists at E0; the owning boundary rejects or structurally excludes the state no later than E0.

diagnostic.remediation: Narrow the Process request to the resolved Sandbox bound.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet A; hook and test locations remain open until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Exec-native extension changes the Sandbox isolation boundary

invariants.title: Platform inferred from the evaluator host
invariants.statement: The Artifact explicitly names its workload operating system, architecture, and target-system contract; evaluator, builder, operator, and runtime host platforms never supply an omitted platform.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare the workload platform explicitly and select only compatible targets.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Non-descriptive profile identity
invariants.statement: Every selectable Artifact profile has a non-empty descriptive behavioral name, and the literal name default is forbidden.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Choose a descriptive behavioral profile name.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Invisible or heuristic profile selection
invariants.statement: Normalization materializes exactly one implicit or explicit profile with pinned name, source, version, digest, and complete expanded semantics; omission selects only the documented product profile and never uses ambient, target, or backend heuristics.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Select or pin one visible profile and materialize its complete expansion.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Descriptive metadata controls another resource
invariants.statement: Artifact metadata is immutable descriptive name, description, and labels only; it neither contains nor controls live identity, timestamps, caller correlation, provider or placement selection, credentials, lifecycle, or policy.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Move the control value to its Artifact policy, Create, operator, service, or live-operation owner.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Untyped or unpinned Nix input identity
invariants.statement: Portable package, devShell, and immutable-input references use typed pinned Nix input, attribute, output, and target-system identities; arbitrary Nix source, functions, evaluator values, raw current-machine store identities, and host paths cannot cross the portable boundary.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than W0.

diagnostic.remediation: Use a typed pinned input, attribute, output, and target-system reference.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Lossy or open-ended devShell projection
invariants.statement: A devShell import projects only packages and closures, explicit non-secret variables, executable search paths, and explicit activation; unsupported, host-dependent, shell-function, interactive-hook, or assumed-service values fail and are never silently dropped or reinterpreted.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at N0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than N0.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep only the supported projection or declare the required behavior through explicit portable fields.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Ambient environment supplies an Artifact default
invariants.statement: The normalized Artifact environment is exactly its explicit variables, canonical package and search-path projection, and activation contract; omitted values remain absent and build, caller, daemon, or host environment never supplies defaults.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare the required non-secret variable or search path explicitly.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Artifact-default cwd outside the Sandbox
invariants.statement: An Artifact-default Process working directory is normalized, absolute, and names a declared permitted in-sandbox path; it is never a current-host, provider, builder, or driver path.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Use an absolute permitted in-sandbox working directory.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Artifact-default Process widens Artifact bounds
invariants.statement: Every populated Artifact-default Process member preserves the Artifact environment, filesystem, identity, resource, and security contracts and never introduces a secret, user, group, privilege, or resource widening.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Narrow the default Process or use the appropriate typed secret or runtime request channel.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Backend-default request in Artifact Process
invariants.statement: After profile expansion, every Artifact-default Process field is explicit, profile-derived, or absent; no portable value or sentinel requests inheritance from an image, provider, target, or backend.
invariants.rationale: A1 can authoritatively reject portable backend-inheritance requests. MAN-004 and Packet C separately prove that target construction preserves an absent value without introducing a backend default.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare the intended Artifact-default Process member explicitly or leave it absent; do not request backend inheritance.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Software or default-Process projection mismatch
invariants.statement: Every built target manifest reproduces the complete normalized software environment and Artifact-default Process metadata exactly and introduces no package, variable, activation, argv, cwd, or user default absent from the Artifact.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at N1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than C0.

diagnostic.remediation: Rebuild the target member from the validated normalized Artifact.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Concrete workspace source or mechanism in Artifact
invariants.statement: The Artifact workspace contains only destination, access ceiling, workload ownership expectations, source requirement, permitted materializations, and a logical slot; checkouts, payloads, host paths, provider objects, volume or snapshot identities, and binding mechanisms belong outside it.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep the logical workspace contract and provide the concrete source through Create.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Workspace requirement and slot disagree
invariants.statement: A required workspace normalizes to exactly one workspace slot whose destination, access ceiling, ownership expectations, cardinality, and allowed materializations equal the workspace contract; an optional workspace cannot manufacture a required binding.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Make the workspace contract and its generated slot identical.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Workspace access folds in lifecycle or result transfer
invariants.statement: Workspace access and materialization requirements are independent of synchronization, writeback, retention, snapshot, capture, and export; those lifecycle and result-transfer choices are not Artifact workspace fields.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Move the lifecycle or result-transfer choice to Create, a live operation, a service, an adapter, or teardown.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Workspace ownership selects host or launcher identity
invariants.statement: Workspace ownership expresses workload-visible UID, GID, or user expectations only; concrete host or guest ID maps, chown strategy, provider identity, and launcher privilege are not Artifact workspace values.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep only workload-visible ownership expectations and move concrete mappings to realization.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Ambiguous filesystem destination topology
invariants.statement: Expanded Artifact filesystem destinations are unambiguous: no two resources claim one destination, and nested destinations require explicit typed composition with deterministic precedence that cannot shadow immutable or protected content.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Use disjoint destinations or an explicit permitted nested composition.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Incomplete or mutable immutable-input contract
invariants.statement: An immutable filesystem input uses a typed pinned or content-addressed source, is Artifact content realized read-only, contains no runtime binding or lifecycle fields, and cannot also claim writable or independent-volume state.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Choose exactly one typed immutable-input, mount-slot, scratch, or volume resource kind.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Incomplete or concrete mount-slot contract
invariants.statement: A filesystem mount slot declares logical identity, source-kind constraint, cardinality, destination, and access ceiling only; it contains no concrete host or provider source and no target-specific mount mechanism.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Complete the logical slot contract and move the concrete source or mechanism to Create or target realization.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Incomplete or externally identified scratch
invariants.statement: Scratch is private writable state scoped to one Sandbox with a destination and hard maximum; it has no external identity, restore, retention, writeback, or create-time actual-size value.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Use scratch for private ephemeral state, a volume slot for independent persistence, or Create for actual allocation.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Concrete or underspecified persistent-volume slot
invariants.statement: A persistent-volume declaration is a logical independent-lifecycle slot with destination, access, cardinality, and capacity bounds; it contains no concrete volume, snapshot, provider identity, attachment mechanism, filesystem driver, or retention operation.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep only the logical volume contract and bind a concrete volume through Create and operator configuration.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Static protected path is invalid or weakened
invariants.statement: Every protected or masked subpath normalizes beneath its declared root, has one non-conflicting immutable protection mode, and cannot be shadowed or widened by another Artifact-declared writable resource.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Normalize the path beneath its root and remove or narrow every shadowing writable resource.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Incomplete or contradictory network authority
invariants.statement: Network authority is one closed explicit policy whose access mode, typed egress rules, DNS behavior, ingress declarations, network credential slots, and required enforcement capability are mutually compatible; no target default fills an omitted policy member.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Choose one complete compatible network policy and declare every required enforcement capability.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Host communication hidden inside network mode
invariants.statement: Unix sockets, vsock, D-Bus, Wayland, PipeWire, brokers, inherited descriptors, and other host channels are individually typed explicit contracts independent of IP network mode; undeclared channels are forbidden.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare each required host channel explicitly or remove it from every target.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Ambiguous resource dimension or enforcement scope
invariants.statement: Every resource bound names a normalized unit, resource dimension, enforcement scope, and bound kind; CPU concurrency, quota, and weight, total and workload memory, task count, root, volume, tmpfs, bandwidth, and IOPS are never interchangeable generic values.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at P1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Select the exact resource dimension, scope, bound kind, and explicit unit.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Artifact resource bounds have an empty range
invariants.statement: Each Artifact resource range is internally satisfiable: all values are positive where required, each minimum is no greater than its hard maximum, and related scoped bounds do not contradict one another.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Choose positive compatible minimum and hard-maximum bounds.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Ambiguous or host-coupled workload identity
invariants.statement: Artifact identity declares deterministic workload-visible user, UID, GID, and supplementary-group constraints only; names resolve inside constructed content, groups are explicit, and host mappings, launcher privilege, provider identity, and ambient groups are forbidden.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare only deterministic workload-visible identity constraints and resolve names from constructed content.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Inconsistent privilege or Linux capability ceiling
invariants.statement: The Artifact privilege ceiling explicitly composes no-new-privileges, privilege escalation, and the permitted Linux capability sets; capability names are canonical, duplicates are forbidden, ambient and inheritable sets cannot exceed permitted bounds, and target defaults cannot add privilege.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Choose a canonical capability ceiling consistent with no-new-privileges and the workload identity.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Unversioned or mechanism-confused kernel security requirement
invariants.statement: Seccomp, LSM, Landlock, syd, namespace, and equivalent kernel-security requirements use registered versioned semantic contracts with explicit architecture and enforcement-strength applicability; one mechanism never stands in for the complete sandbox policy.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Use a registered versioned semantic requirement and declare every separate required security property.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Concrete or underspecified device requirement
invariants.statement: An Artifact device requirement declares a logical device class, count, access, isolation, and capability contract only; it contains no live device identity, host path, IOMMU group, provider allocation, or placement choice.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep a logical device contract and supply concrete allocation through Create, operator, and host preflight.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Device injection edits undeclared Artifact semantics
invariants.statement: A device or CDI-style requirement explicitly projects every environment, mount, hook, group, capability, and host-channel effect into the corresponding Artifact contract; opaque device names cannot smuggle additional authority.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Project and validate every device-induced edit or reject the device contract.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Incomplete secret delivery alternative
invariants.statement: Every secret slot declares a non-empty set of typed delivery alternatives, and each alternative contains exactly the destination, audience, ownership or mode, lifetime, and snapshot constraints meaningful for that delivery kind.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Choose a typed delivery alternative and complete only its applicable contract fields.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Secret destination conflicts with another resource
invariants.statement: A secret destination cannot simultaneously be ordinary environment, immutable content, a declared output, protected control-only content, or another incompatible single-writer destination.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Move the secret to one declared ephemeral secret channel with a non-conflicting destination.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Secret and snapshot contracts disagree
invariants.statement: When a supported snapshot class can capture a secret-delivery surface, both the secret slot and snapshot requirement explicitly and compatibly state whether inclusion is forbidden or permitted.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Make secret inclusion explicit and compatible in both contracts.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Unsatisfied or contradictory capability requirement
invariants.statement: Every required capability has a registered or namespaced identity, compatible version constraint, explicit requirement strength, and satisfiable dependency closure; required and merely advertised states cannot conflict.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Use compatible registered capability versions and satisfy every required dependency.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Incomplete snapshot capability contract
invariants.statement: A snapshot requirement names its component set and explicitly states external-storage, secret, compatibility-domain, and quiescing treatment; memory inclusion also states device-state treatment.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare the complete semantic capture contract rather than a snapshot or persistence boolean.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Conflated persistence semantics
invariants.statement: Scratch, persistent-volume binding requirements, snapshot or restore capability requirements, workspace synchronization, and declared-output capture are distinct resource kinds; no generic persistence, snapshot, hibernation, changes, or writeback boolean aliases them.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Select the separate resource contract that matches storage, snapshot, synchronization, or output intent.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Incomplete or runtime-owned output declaration
invariants.statement: Every declared output has a unique identity, normalized exact in-sandbox path, and explicit file or directory kind; it contains no host or provider export destination, per-run selection, capture timing, retention, or required-existence policy.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep only the output convention and choose capture, destination, timing, and retention in a runtime operation.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Declared output conflicts with filesystem policy
invariants.statement: A declared-output path is reachable through the Artifact filesystem contract and does not incompatibly overlap secret delivery, protected control-only content, or immutable-only content.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Place the output on a declared writable reachable path that does not cross a protected or secret boundary.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Portable semantic identity includes non-semantic provenance
invariants.statement: The portable semantic digest includes fully expanded Artifact semantics and pinned profile identity, version, and content digest, but excludes selector explicitness, source spans, formatting, checkout path, timestamps, and field-level explanation provenance.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at W0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than W0.

diagnostic.remediation: Hash only normalized semantics and pinned semantic dependencies; retain explanation data outside the digest domain.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Artifact identity domains are interchanged
invariants.statement: Portable semantic digest, target-member content digests, and Artifact Set identity are typed distinct identity domains and are never substituted or compared as interchangeable values.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at N1; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than C0.

diagnostic.remediation: Use the expected typed identity domain and verify every member and set relationship.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Invalid target or runtime-profile declaration
invariants.statement: Enabled target and runtime-profile identities are unique, explicit, registered or namespaced, and each runtime profile is attached only to a compatible enabled target.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Use unique registered target and runtime-profile identities with compatible associations.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Divergent common semantics share one Artifact identity
invariants.statement: Every target member in one Artifact Set preserves one identical common Artifact contract; intentionally different common environment, workspace, policy, resource, or requirement semantics are separate named Artifact Definitions with distinct semantic identities.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Split divergent behavior into separate named Artifact Definitions that may import one shared module.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Artifact-native configuration has the wrong scope
invariants.statement: Artifact-native configuration is accepted only under an enabled target and a registered versioned artifact-construction namespace; data for a disabled target, unknown namespace, or Create, operator, service, live, Exec, framework, or runtime scope is rejected rather than ignored.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Move the value to a registered versioned construction namespace under its enabled target or to its actual lifecycle owner.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Byte-changing native input is unpinned or unhashed
invariants.statement: Every native input capable of changing constructed bytes resolves through a typed pinned handle before construction and participates in the affected target-member identity.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at N0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than N0.

diagnostic.remediation: Use a registered typed pinned native handle and include its resolved identity in the affected target member.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Invalid or weakened Artifact lifetime ceiling
invariants.statement: An Artifact maximum lifetime, when present, is a positive finite hard security ceiling; composition may only narrow it, omission means no Artifact-imposed ceiling, and no target default is imported into Artifact semantics.
invariants.rationale: The complete normalized Artifact information needed for this Packet B rule first exists at A0; the authoritative boundary rejects it no later than A1.

diagnostic.remediation: Use a positive finite ceiling, narrow it monotonically, or omit it explicitly.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet B; hook and test locations remain planned until implementation tracing.

invariants.title: Target manifest incompletely projects portable semantics
invariants.statement: Every target-member manifest reproduces the complete normalized Artifact contract, explicit absences, target-realization requirements, and default-suppression obligations across every portable field family.
invariants.rationale: The complete built projection first exists at N1. Manifest load must compare it with the normalized common contract before any Create selection can trust the member.

diagnostic.remediation: Rebuild the target member from the normalized Artifact and emit the complete projection, explicit absences, requirements, and default-suppression obligations.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C while expanding all 81 Artifact fields across four initial runtime profiles.

invariants.title: Incompatible runtime profiles share one member manifest
invariants.statement: Byte-identical content blobs may be deduplicated, but one member manifest may advertise multiple runtime profiles only when builder evidence independently proves each profile compatible with that exact member and their immutable hard requirements are identical.
invariants.rationale: Only the completed members and their profile requirement graphs reveal whether sharing preserves identity and hard requirements. Manifest load must reject false sharing before Create.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep reusable content blobs deduplicated but emit separate member manifests for profiles with different immutable hard requirements.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C from Firecracker and Cloud Hypervisor device, helper, workspace, snapshot, and protocol differences.

invariants.title: Runtime implementation mismatches the selected profile bundle
invariants.statement: Host preflight verifies the selected profile's exact registered implementation bundle, executable revisions, build features, mandatory helpers, process confinement, kernel facilities, and conformance versions before launch.
invariants.rationale: Builder evidence describes a compatible profile, but only host preflight can identify the concrete executable variants, helpers, kernel support, and process confinement selected for this launch.

diagnostic.remediation: Select a host and registered implementation bundle matching every pinned component, feature, helper, confinement, kernel, and conformance requirement; do not fall back.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C from non-setuid Bubblewrap, Firecracker jailer, and Cloud Hypervisor outer-confinement requirements.

invariants.title: Dynamic filesystem source changes after preflight
invariants.statement: Every dynamic filesystem source is safely resolved to an object identity retained through target attachment; validation by pathname followed by a later pathname reopen is forbidden.
invariants.rationale: The concrete source exists only on the selected host. Retaining its verified object identity across the preflight-to-driver handoff is required to prevent path replacement and symlink traversal races.

diagnostic.remediation: Resolve the source safely, retain a descriptor or equivalent stable object handle through attachment, and reject any identity change.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C from Bubblewrap FD-bind support and Cloud Hypervisor trusted-caller path-resolution requirements.

invariants.title: Snapshot or restore violates its proven compatibility envelope
invariants.statement: Every snapshot or restore operation revalidates the exact captured component set, external-storage state, device state, secret treatment, quiescing state, VMM/driver/guest/kernel/CPU compatibility, and clone identity refresh required by the advertised snapshot class.
invariants.rationale: The Artifact and member can define and advertise a snapshot class, but only the live-operation boundary knows resident secrets, current devices/storage, quiescing, restore host, and clone count.

diagnostic.remediation: Quiesce and scrub as required, use a compatible restore envelope, rebind runtime identities, and refresh clone identity state before capture or resume.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C from Firecracker and Cloud Hypervisor component, compatibility, secret, and clone-safety limitations.

invariants.title: Provider transfer substitutes an unverifiable object
invariants.statement: Provider transport preserves portable semantic identity and verifies selected member bytes or the OCI descriptor graph by digest after upload, download, and every cache hit; provider object IDs, aliases, tags, paths, and cache keys remain non-semantic metadata.
invariants.rationale: The selected member identity is known earlier, but only provider preflight can observe the transferred or cached object returned for this request and verify its content graph.

diagnostic.remediation: Reject the provider object and transfer or fetch the exact member or OCI descriptor graph by verified content identity.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C provider research; transport is explicitly not a target profile.

invariants.title: Provider-side construction lacks equivalence evidence
invariants.statement: Provider-side construction may claim portable conformance only through a versioned product construction protocol with complete pinned inputs, suppressed provider defaults, a returned output identity, provenance, and member-bound semantic and runtime conformance evidence.
invariants.rationale: The versioned construction protocol and pinned input set are known when remote target-member construction begins. The provider output identity and evidence exist at N1 and must be verified before a member is published or can reach manifest verification at C0.

diagnostic.remediation: Use the versioned product construction protocol and require pinned inputs, explicit default suppression, output identity, provenance, and conformance evidence; otherwise expose the provider path as explicitly non-conforming.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C from Modal/E2B-style provider construction boundaries.

invariants.title: Frontend dependency closure is mutable or incomplete
invariants.statement: Every semantic import, module, resource, external reader, fallback, and native source input belongs to one transitively immutable, content-pinned, provenance-recorded dependency closure that evaluates offline deterministically.
invariants.rationale: A frontend can identify its complete semantic dependency closure at P1; canonical publication at W0 is the latest safe boundary for independently verifying that closure and its identity.

diagnostic.remediation: Pin and record the complete transitive dependency closure, remove ambient readers and fallback imports, and evaluate offline.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D frontend and Nix composition research.

invariants.title: Composition provenance is incomplete
invariants.statement: Normalized composition provenance records every winning, losing, default, profile, import, override, native, and migration contributor with immutable identity and semantic role while excluding display-only source spans and order from the semantic digest.
invariants.rationale: All contributors and their roles are known after final Artifact composition at A1 and must be complete before canonical publication at W0.

diagnostic.remediation: Regenerate provenance from the complete contribution ledger and keep display-only locations outside the semantic digest.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D strongest-bypass analysis.

invariants.title: Extension effect projection is incomplete
invariants.statement: Every extension used by a conforming Artifact has a registered versioned closed contract and a total product-derived effect projection into the common field/profile and identity models; opaque or unprojectable effects cannot produce conforming types or claims.
invariants.rationale: Extension scope and declared effects are known at A1; target construction at N0 is the last boundary with both the resolved native value and the complete Packet C realization model.

diagnostic.remediation: Use a registered extension with a complete product-derived effect projection or emit an explicitly non-conforming output type.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D native-surface analysis.

invariants.title: Frontend translation is lossy or permissive
invariants.statement: Every renderer-to-wire adaptation is versioned and total over the semantic schema and fails closed on unknown, omitted, unserializable, rounded, duplicated, or reinterpreted values.
invariants.rationale: Only the W0 adapter boundary has both the rendered frontend value and the exact current wire schema, so it must prove a lossless total translation before canonicalization.

diagnostic.remediation: Use the version-matched total adapter and reject every value that cannot be represented exactly in the canonical schema.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D by tracing the comparison portable-value projection.

invariants.title: Canonical decoding is unbounded or accepts an invalid domain
invariants.statement: Canonical decoding rejects malformed syntax, trailing bytes, invalid UTF-8, unsupported numeric or Unicode representations, excessive nesting, and oversized input before semantic interpretation; WIRE-001 separately owns duplicate-object-key rejection.
invariants.rationale: Raw bytes and configured decoder bounds first meet at W0, and no partial or implementation-dependent interpretation may cross that boundary.

diagnostic.remediation: Encode one bounded canonical document in the supported byte, numeric, and Unicode domain.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D raw-wire boundary analysis.

invariants.title: Schema migration is ambiguous or non-idempotent
invariants.statement: Each supported old schema version has one versioned deterministic migration that validates old input first, preserves or explicitly rejects extension data, validates the current result, and is idempotent; downgrade, fallback chains, and frontend-owned migration are forbidden.
invariants.rationale: The original version and complete decoded old value first meet the product-owned migration registry at W0, where migration must finish before current canonical validation.

diagnostic.remediation: Use the single registered source-to-current migration and resolve every loss, ambiguity, or unsupported extension explicitly.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D migration-boundary analysis.

invariants.title: Native handle identity is incomplete
invariants.statement: A native handle identity binds the complete pinned transitive source graph, registry namespace and version, export attribute, native interface version, target system, affected member, and expected semantic effect; one registry-file digest or a current store path is insufficient.
invariants.rationale: The complete native registry, transitive Nix source closure, target system, export contract, and affected member first meet at N0 and must be bound before derivation construction.

diagnostic.remediation: Regenerate the typed handle identity over the complete transitive source and interface tuple for the exact target system and affected member.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D by tracing the native-handle prototype identity domain.

invariants.title: Operator Configuration dependency closure is mutable or incomplete
invariants.statement: Operator Configuration dependency closure is mutable, incomplete, ambient, or not reproducible offline.
invariants.rationale: OC0 is the first boundary with the fully composed Operator Configuration and its dependency closure; it must reject non-reproducible or ambient composition before admission.

diagnostic.remediation: Pin every dependency, evaluate offline without ambient inputs, and submit the closed result to OC0.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Operator Configuration precedence or provenance is ambiguous
invariants.statement: Operator composition precedence or contributor provenance is ambiguous, incomplete, or permits a force-class bypass.
invariants.rationale: OC0 is the first boundary with the complete Operator contributor ledger and precedence result; it must reject ambiguity and force-class bypasses there.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare every contributor and precedence decision, and reject undeclared force-class overrides at OC0.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Operator Configuration escapes final validation
invariants.statement: A native/freeform source escape constructs validated Operator Configuration without the OC0 validator.
invariants.rationale: OC0 is the only boundary that can turn a fully composed Operator candidate into validated configuration; native/freeform input cannot bypass it.

diagnostic.remediation: Route native/freeform input through OC0; only the validator may construct validated Operator Configuration.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Managed-Service Definition dependency closure is mutable or incomplete
invariants.statement: Managed-Service Definition dependency closure is mutable, incomplete, ambient, or not reproducible offline.
invariants.rationale: MS0 is the first boundary with the fully composed Managed-Service Definition and its dependency closure; it must reject non-reproducible or ambient composition before translation.

diagnostic.remediation: Pin every dependency, evaluate offline without ambient inputs, and submit the closed result to MS0.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Service precedence or provenance is ambiguous
invariants.statement: Service composition precedence or contributor provenance is ambiguous, incomplete, or permits a force-class bypass.
invariants.rationale: MS0 is the first boundary with the complete Service contributor ledger and precedence result; it must reject ambiguity and force-class bypasses there.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare every contributor and precedence decision, and reject undeclared force-class overrides at MS0.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Managed-Service Definition escapes final validation or the Core API
invariants.statement: A native/freeform source escape constructs a validated Managed-Service Definition or direct driver action without MS0 and the typed Core API.
invariants.rationale: MS0 is the only boundary that can turn a fully composed Service candidate into a validated definition; native/freeform input cannot bypass it or invoke a driver directly.

diagnostic.remediation: Route native/freeform input through MS0 and the typed Core API; direct driver action is unsupported.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Serialized resolved-stage envelope is open or ambiguously decoded
invariants.statement: A serialized resolved-stage envelope is open, unbounded, ambiguously decoded, unsupported, or accepted without strict versioned decoding.
invariants.rationale: RW0 is the first boundary with the serialized reentry envelope; strict bounded versioned decoding must reject it before replay.

diagnostic.remediation: Use the closed, bounded, versioned reentry envelope and strictly decode it at RW0 before full replay.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Reentry mints a private validated runtime stage
invariants.statement: Deserialization, copying, a cache hit, or a foreign object mints a private validated runtime stage.
invariants.rationale: RW0 bytes can produce only an untrusted candidate; C0 is the first product constructor permitted to mint a fresh private stage after complete replay.

diagnostic.remediation: Strictly decode and fully replay the reentry candidate; mint a private stage only through the C0 product constructor.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: PreparedLaunch identity fails to rederive upstream bindings
invariants.statement: PreparedLaunch identity omits or fails to rederive an earlier product identity, registration, admission, or retained-object binding.
invariants.rationale: D0 is the final preparation boundary with the current retained-object bindings and the complete PreparedLaunch identity; it must rederive them before driver use.

diagnostic.remediation: Rederive PreparedLaunch identity from every upstream product identity, registration, admission, and retained-object binding.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Driver accepts non-private or raw configuration input
invariants.statement: A driver accepts anything other than the product-owned private PreparedLaunch stage or accepts raw/backend-default configuration as input.
invariants.rationale: D0 is the driver-entry boundary; only the product-owned private PreparedLaunch type is admissible and raw/backend-default input has no supported construction path.

diagnostic.remediation: Invoke drivers only with the product-owned private PreparedLaunch and reject direct, raw, copied, deserialized, or backend-default input before mutation.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.
